Nathan NS5113-0478-00 StrobeLight - Lime Punch/Classic Green A compact little visibility light, quite useful if you are running at night and want something to tell drivers that you are around. Superior to a simple reflective vest, especially with a blinking pattern. Not so useful at dusk though - the light simply isn't bright enough to draw a lot of attention when the ambient light is still high. This isn't a significant issue, just don't expect it to do something too substantial.

The interface is pretty good - a long press ensures that it will almost never be activated accidentally, it is easy to switch between modes, and the light remembers the last mode you were on. The blinking patterns are variegated and should draw notice from drivers. The clip is perfect for non-intrusive mounting to a belt, arm band, or pack strap.

I would recommend this for night runners, so long as it compliments a reflective vest and reflective wrist/ankle bands. I use it as a a rear pack light when hiking, since the pack hides my reflective vest. The lithium battery and long lifespan make this an ideal light to tuck away in your hiking pack just in case you end up on the road at night.

text_fidelity_a:
VINTEX Portable Camping Shower, Portable Shower with USB Rechargeable Battery, Outdoor Shower for Hiking, Traveling, Pet Bath I have had camp showers before, but they have always been manual pumps so I never had to figure out the electronics of a pump like this. I want to prevent frustration that I had in running this by giving you detailed instructions on how to work this. It is too nice of a pump to miss out on.

INSTRUCTIONS
There were absolutely no instructions with this. I was frustrated.

MOTOR
Make sure that the little black motor has the suction cup attachment slid onto the bottom rails of the pump. There is a cord attached to the motor that will be plugged INTO THE BATTERY PACK to run it later.

ROCKER SWITCH
Be sure that this switch is in the off position.

POWER BANK
There is an electrical plug that plugs into the round hole of the power bank. It says that it will charge very fast, but I found that it took over an hour to get to the point where I could have 2 bars on the bank.

READY TO USE IT?
I used this in a 5 gallon bucket. I filled it with warm water about 3/4 of the way up.

PICK WHAT SHOWER HEAD
You have a sprayer like the kitchen sprayer on a sink or a nice shower head to choose from.

INSTALL WASHER
There is a silicone ring available for each sprayer head. I highly suggest that you attach any extras to the cord with the twist tie so it won't get lost. You can also try installing the ring into each head and hope they don't fall out.

SCREW ON
Once the washer is installed, screw the hose onto the shower head. Then screw the other end onto the pump. No need for a washer there because it will be under water.

ROCKER SWITCH
Make sure that the rocker switch is in the OFF position. When the power bank is charged the light on the charging plug will turn from red to green. Once it is ready, plug the power bank (make sure that the power button is in the off position) and keep it away from the water so it does not accidentally get wet.

TURN ON
Using the rocker switch, turn on the pump. The water will come out pretty quickly so be ready.

HOW TO CHECK BATTERY
To check the battery status on the power bank, turn the switch to the on position and it will show with blue lights how much power is left.

TIME
There is about 60 minutes of showering to a charge on the power bank, depending on how often it is turned off in between sprays.

PERFORMANCE
This is one of the nicest portable showers I have tried. The water pressure is fantastic and really does perform like a shower. The hose is long enough to use this in a shower tent. The rocker switch is handy so that you can turn it on and off preserving battery for longer usage.

I love that you can use whatever water source you have handy as long as it does not have debris in it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Despite being very frustrated at first, once I figured out how to use this, I really love it. I hope my instructions can help anyone else not be frustrated so you can just enjoy the shower.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS for performance, but honestly the lack of instructions in the box makes me want to take off a star or two. I won't for now.
text_fidelity_b: VINTEX Portable Camping Shower, Portable Shower with USB Rechargeable Battery, Outdoor Shower for Hiking, Traveling, Pet Bath

Right now I'm on a bit of a budget, so decided to go with the lower-featured FT1. I have to say I have been pleasantly surprised. After a little learning curve with the 1-button controls, I've found it easy to use, informative and the audible alarm is helpful.

The only thing I didn't love about my Polar FT1 was the chest strap it comes with. The higher end Polars come with a softer fabric strap, but the FT1 comes with a strap with a sort of flexible plastic piece on the front that isn't as form-fitting. It's not terrible - honest! - but it's not great, either. I ended up getting a Polar H7, and it works great with my FT1 plus I can simultaneously use it with various fitness apps on my phone; I like it best with Endomondo, which also sends your workout to My Fitness Pal.

The features I was looking for that the FT1 has:
A large-ish, easy to read display
An alarm you can set so you're alerted when your heart rate gets too high or too low during workouts
The ability to change your max heart rate
Comfortable wrist band

Overall I'm happy with my FT1, and even happier when I paired it with the Polar H7, but honestly it works fine with the strap it came with. I may upgrade someday, but for now my FT1 has/does everything I need and works great.

The hat itself is lightweight, comfortable, and breathable. The brim really does fold so you can stuff the hat in a bag without it taking up a lot of space. The hat is not adjustable in the normal sense, you can’t make it tighter. The back band is elastic, not a sliding buckle.

The mesh portion to protect the face and back of the neck is somewhat flimsy, and honestly, I am worried how much sun it actually blocks. The mesh is transparent, I can see my face underneath it. So I still put on sunscreen.

I did discover the mesh portion can be stuffed inside the hat and I can still wear the hat on my head. So if I needed the mesh and then didn’t need it, I can just hide it away in the hat and not worry about losing or unsnapping it.

Sigma BC2006MHR DTS Wireless Bicycle Speedometer with Heart Rate Monitor and Altimeter I've had this unit for 6 months. It pretty much works as advertised, but-battery life and magnet strength in Xmitter is questionable. The sender has to be about 1-2 mm from the battery. That's a pretty tight fit, esp with carbon front forks. As the battery on the sender weakens, there's no real communication from it to tell what the problem is (I got a "Too Many Signals" error). On the computer unit, Temperature gauge isn't accurate, reads way too high, and there doesn't seem to be any way to calibrate it. The manual is thorough and detailed, but somehow confusing (What can I say? It's written by English speakers, not English thinkers)
On the positive side, The readout is very clear; you can do individual parameter resets, the rubber bands (o-rings really) are pretty tough, I haven't broken one yet, and it has a dual mount, stem or handlebar, which was very important for me, as I put safety brakes on my handle bar, which ate up real estate. At 120 bucks, it's pricey, but at 83? IMO that's getting into bargain territory for the feature set.

Buy this only if you want an unsharpened practice kama. Seller really needs to update the picture.

Needs to be packaged better, but at least it was still undamaged, which proves the materials are suitably sturdy. I don't know if it will stand up to a real impact, though.

text_fidelity_a:
Stamina 3-in-1 Core Training System, Gray This may not be the most versatile machine, making this less of a must for your home gym, but I like it anyway!

Some reviewers noted problems for taller people, but since my house is full of short people, myself included, none of us had issues.

Setup is pretty quick and easy, as is use and adjusting for various activities. The ab crunching sliding thing in the front is a great workout for the whole core (though more twisting is better for obliques and a narrower waistline, so word of caution at doing it too much, as you might add some bulk to the waist). Using it to do regular crunches on the bench or twisting crunches (I like those better) is nice, since ones feet tend to want to lift off the ground, and the incline position is even more of a challenge for advanced people.

And yes, as a bench, it helps give a stable base for free weights. I didn’t really have a sitting place in my home gym, so this is helpful for that, as well as for silly stuff like putting on and taking off shoes.

Honestly, if you have a medium sized home gym, this is a nice thing to have. With my current collection consisting of an elliptical machine, bike, free weights, a bosu ball (the half ball on a plastic flat thing—very versatile!, and a fitness ball, I’d say my home gym is pretty much complete!

Custom Gambler Professional Table Tennis Paddle with ThermoPoly (TP) Carbon Blade and Wraith Rubber Plus Paddle Case I would classify myself as a beginnermediate player. I can hold my own but rarely beat an advanced player. When I started, I was using the community paddles at work which are usually in rough shape. Those are all kit type Stiga or other generic paddle set paddles you can get from any sporting goods store. I couldn't do anything but rely on a defensive style of play which was really tough against the better players.

When I realized I needed my own paddle, I searched and searched and eventually settled on the Killerspin JET300. But just before purchasing I decided to look up as much as I could. I stumbled on the reviews for this paddle and weren't sure what to make of it. Then I went outside of Amazon and read up some more on Gambler paddles. Because of the price and based on the consistently positive reviews, I decided to go for it. I asked the seller for a red paddle case (which was included) and they happily replied that they would do so. When the paddle arrived, it came in perfectly setup, clean and super tacky. Unlike some of the other paddles I've tried including several different KillerSpin, Stiga, and DHS racquets, mine turns the ball really well in every direction. The edges of the rubbers did come a little loose after about two months but they're meant to be replaced. That would be my only con but not enough to even reduce the rating of this review.

That being said... in summary... great rubbers included and excellent build. Service from the vendor was also excellent. The racquet itself is weighted toward the medium end, maybe a little heavy from the middle but not heavy. The racquet is not fast by any means... you'll need to drive the ball to get it to really move, but it's doable. Was so impressed with the racquet that I bought 3 dozen 3-star balls from Gambler (which are also very good).
text_fidelity_b: Custom Gambler Professional Table Tennis Paddle with ThermoPoly (TP) Carbon Blade and Wraith Rubber Plus Paddle Case

Horse Hair Fly Whisk I love this, my horses love it and the bugs hate it! You can fly spray your horse till it's drenched, but, those darn deerflies and other nasty bugs like to zero in on the horses. This is a very well made, VERY reasonably priced alternative that works! I've had biting bugs that were under my horse's belly that they kept kicking at and with this whisk I can even reach down and shoo them away. It also reaches back to their flank without a problem. In fact, there is no place this won't reach. The only time you might have to bend over is to get one that is at their feet area.

Some desensitizing to the horse may be necessary before using. My horses had a lot of desensitizing done beforehand and needed no time at all to get used to this, but, I have had others who got one because I had it and it works so well but their horses were afraid of it.

You have to know your horse. It is something I would highly recommend getting your horse used if they are afraid of it so that it can be used. I highly recommend this product and I won't ride without it. And yes, you can use a small tree branch with leaves for the same purpose, but, I like that I can just hang this from my saddle horn and not have to look for a good branch along the way anymore. LOVE this product!
text_fidelity_b: Horse Hair Fly Whisk

This was the one we got her and so far, we really like it. I normally do not talk about price points, but in this case: for the price point it feels, looks, and acts like a solid choice. We hope to never have to find out about the "protective" elements, but hope it holds up to that standard as well.

1. The Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light is a good looking helmet, so if looks are important, this has a nice look to it. We like the blue we picked and the overall look is cool.

2. The fit is good. My wife has a smaller head than mine, so we got one that was very adjustable - not really by choice in that we would have order one "size specific" if needed, but again, for her needs. In this case, the Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light allows you to adjust the size in a "one size fits all" situation. The dial on the back adjusts for you and so far it works well. She likes the fit she gets and feels comfortable between that adjustment and the strap.

3. There is no way to "test" this helmet without falling - and we are not test dummies - so we must trust this will have the good if ever needed. She took a good spill once off a SEGWAY and had a helmet on - which truly saved her - and so we swear by wearing head gear. Here I jump to the idea of "You get what you pay for." The helmet we were able to get for me was a far higher price (here on Amazon, over $200), and you CAN tell a difference. BUT, that said, compared to our previous, similarly priced helmets, this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light does seem to have what we need. Would we upgrade? Sure, who wouldn't? BUT, if price is a concern, and for most of us it is, would this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light do the trick? WE THINK SO. Again, there is NO way to know until you need it. BUT this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light fits like the ones we have had in the past and has a similar feel, so we are "trusting" it to take care of her if ever needed.

4. The inside lining IS thinner than mine. There is a difference in that kind of thing - bringing us back to, if we had the money we WOULD upgrade. But for what it is, this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light feels good on her head and she is comfortable.

5. The lights on the back are a huge bonus and work really well. There are (I think) 3 settings for different flashing options and we love that she can do this to bring attention to herself. That said, we have no intention of being out at night, but even in the daylight, it IS something that catches your eye.

In the end and overall we are very pleased with this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light and are happy to have it. Does price matter? You tell me. Yes, there IS a difference for a MUCH higher price point. But if the idea is to get something good on your head to keep you. safe, we think this Westt Road – Bike Helmet for Adults with Integrated LED Light offers us a great option.

I mention this as I have had or used different camping air mattresses through the years & sometimes you had to battle a little to get them in their travel bags. About 12 inches long & 7 inches wide when folded in bag. Actually was more comfortable than I thought it would be. The one thing that could use a better design is the pump. Directions say open valve & pump with foot. Your foot goes over the hole, so you kind of have to lift your foot a little for it to inflate, if you leave your foot over valve, it doesn’t allow air in to inflate. I think that could of been designed a little better. I also had my son give it a try. He is taller than me & had a few inches to spare, as he may be the one to use it sometimes, nice to know it will still work for him as he grows. Decent air mattress, happy with this order.

Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I purchased this unit mainly for the continuous heart rate recording. It seems to do that very well.

The most amazing thing about this Charge HR is the quality of the software - both the user interface and the signal processing. It's impressive that it figures out when I'm "outdoor cycling" and that it identifies a racquetball game as "Sport".

It's not so great that it isn't waterproof and that the battery lasts only about a day with all features activated. As clever as the makers of this device are, how difficult would it be for them to build a waterproof version with batter battery life?

The unit won't sync without an internet connection for your linked device, as far as I can tell. This can be important if you want to change a setting on the device and are not in an internet coverage area. Fitbit talks to your phone via Bluetooth, and you would think that would be enough, but sync won't happen until your linked device is connected to the internet.

On balance, I'm blown away with what this little Fitbit Charge HR can do and wouldn't want to give it up!

text_fidelity_a: Confidence Fitness Slim Full Body Vibration Platform Fitness Machine, Black My husband and I bought this piece of equipment to add to our existing exercise equipment, and with the hope that it might boost my low bone density a bit.  I've been using it about 3 times a week for several months now, and while I don't think there is any weight loss (did not want it for that anyway), I definitely feel better after I've been on it for 10 minutes.  When I first started using it, I would stand with my feet about 14-15 inches apart, and an hour or so later would feel my back hurting a bit and I couldn't have the speed any higher than about 5 or 6.  So figured out that since this oscillates up and down from left to right (like a superfast see-saw), I would try standing with my feet much closer together.  The up and down movement would be greatly lessened so it wouldn't put so much pressure on the back after the 10 minute stand.  This worked beautifully and now as long as I keep my feet only about 4" apart I can turn the speed up much higher, it seems to eliminate residual stress in my system, and my back does not hurt at all after using it.  So how you place your feet and your posture also is very important in how you will feel after using this vibration plate.  I have yet to get my bone density rechecked so not sure if it has helped that or not, but I really like this machine a lot, am very glad we bought it and plan to keep using it for as long as it lasts.
text_fidelity_b: Confidence Fitness Slim Full Body Vibration Platform Fitness Machine, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Coast DX355 Double Lock Folding Knife I've been looking for a folding knife that I could use around the farm. This knife is 4.5 inches long and 1.5 inches wide when folded, so it has a nice sized blade while still being small enough not to get in my way when clipped onto my pocket. (There is a strong, nearly 3-inch-long metal clip securely screwed into the knife handle.) The entire knife appears to be made out of a sturdy, stainless steel. The handle has a texture and finger indentations to assure a secure grip when used.

I've never used a folding knife with a locking mechanism, but I expected at least some advertising pointing out how the special double-locking mechanism works. There wasn't any information included with the knife, but it was fairly easy to figure out. The linear lock is beneath the blade and automatically locks when the blade is fully extended. The safety switch is a toggle on the handle behind the blade. You can push it up when the blade is open to prevent the linear lock from being depressed (which would allow the blade to close). To close the blade, push the toggle back to the original position and depress the linear lock while folding the blade. Once I figured it out, it was easy to do.

Since it's winter, I haven't had much time to test the blade out for how well it keeps it edge or other wear issues. I'll post an update is anything significant comes up.
text_fidelity_b: Coast DX355 Double Lock Folding Knife

Best Self Inflating Sleeping pad Lightweight Camping Foam pad- Best for Camping Backpacking & Hiking. R Value of 4.9 - Inflatable Camping Mattress I do a lot of camping of all kinds and have had many pads over the years, from expensive brand name ones to $10 foam pads from a gas station in the middle of nowhere.

Don't buy this if you think it's the same thing as a brand name pad at less than half the cost. It does well, but has some significant disadvantages. Read on for more detail.

Successfully imitates the more expensive pads in:
* Comfort - it's thick and it's soft.
* Warmth - it's thickness and foaminess insulates decently well.
* Durability - time will tell, but it appears to be made of a thick sturdy material.
* Reasonably small.

Here is where this pad falls short:
* It's big and heavy when compressed. Almost twice the size of the brand name pads. I'd think twice about using this for backpacking if you plan on going far or fast.
* The valve sucks. Most good pads have a valve that can be close by snapping it in, this one will let air out while you spin it shut.
* The foam/insulation is cheap - meaning it's not as warm as a comparable pad of the same weight. Probably fine down to freezing temps though.
* The material is very plasticky and doesn't have a very pleasant feel to it. I know this is nitpicking, but you're going to be sleeping on this after all, it should be pleasant.
text_fidelity_b: Best Self Inflating Sleeping pad Lightweight Camping Foam pad- Best for Camping Backpacking & Hiking. R Value of 4.9 - Inflatable Camping Mattress

This replicates that experience or rather it replicates the Kan Jam game. As with all variants, its easy to learn and makes for great backyard fun for parties and gatherings. Most folks have some level of Frisbee skills, and most folks have played a game with a goal/goalie. This piggy-backs off of that common knowledge.

While the game is fun, the parts in this kit are basic. This helps keep the cost down and keeps it highly portable. Both are sound choices, but it would feel better if the actual cost were a bit lower. I'm thinking $25-30 more than close to $40. Price aside, it doesn't take up that much space when storing, and it's looking plenty durable.

I'd definitely recommend checking out Kan Jam and related Frisbee games. They're fun! As far as the hardware, this is definitely something I can recommend, but I cannot see why this would be better than another competing product.

text_fidelity_a:
Ibera Bicycle Bag PakRak Clip-On Quick-Release All Weather Bike Panniers (Pair), Includes Rain Cover , Black These are nice looking and well constructed panniers. However, they have a few issues that leave me not fully satisfied.

First, there is not a single hook, loop, strap, or D ring for you to attach anything to. No place to attach a reflector or a tail light, no place to attach bungees, nothing. Seriously? Has whoever designed these every ridden a bike? There's always something you want to attach somewhere. How hard is it to add a few strategically placed D rings and maybe a strap for a clip-on light?

Second, other than the very flat zippered pocket on the top flap, there is not a divider or a pocket anywhere, inside or out. Everything you put in this pannier is just bouncing around with everything else in there. I like to keep my tools, my spare inner tube, a rag, a few wipes and a few zip ties with me at all times. I'd like to keep all these supplies in a pocket separate from my groceries, laptop, .... But no. There's not a pocket anywhere for a road kit. I had to buy ditty bags and put my emergency kit in those, and toss those in the bottom of these bags, where they continue to bounce around with everything else. But at least they bounce around together.

Third, I find these bags unnecessarily difficult to close. There's a bit of elastic at the back of the cover, near the rack, that does not glide smoothly over the body of the bag. Every single time I close these bags, I have to grab the elastic on both sides and pull it into place for a snug fit. It does make the bag look nice and neat when closed, and maybe it helps keep rain out. But it's annoying that I can't just flip the flap over and close the bag. Also, the clips that hold the top flap down are surprisingly finicky. I'm not sure why, but I have to slide the tab into the clip exactly parallel or it won't go in.

Fourth, the bags do not collapse when empty.They ship flat, and I assumed that I could collapse them at least a little bit when they're empty. But no. They ship with rigid pieces of plastic that you slide into very snug slots to give them structure and shape. You do not want to remove these every time you empty the bag and reinsert them when you load the bag. And even if you did remove them, the bag would just flop around loosely - you can't cinch it so it's smaller. So these bags are always the same (generous) size no matter how much or how little you have in them.

Finally, the bag claims to fit most racks. IT DOES NOT. The clips on top probably do fit over a variety of sizes of rack tubes. And the tab that releases the top clips is a really nice touch, and works well. The problem is the bottom clip, the one that keeps the bag from flapping around when you turn. It is a fixed distance from the top clips, and the distance is very short! I saw that before I purchased these, but I thought I'd be able to rotate the clip so it could grab on to one of the tubes going down to the bottom of my rack. WRONG. That clip does not move up or down, and it does not rotate - you can only slide it left and right. So if the bottom tube of your rack isn't exactly 7" from the top tube, the bottom clip won't connect. I had to remove the bottom clip, flip it upside down, then use a 10" bungee to stretch between the bottom tube of my rack and the inverted clip on this bag. It's a reasonably snug fit and it works well enough. But, contrary to its claims, this bag did not fit my rack - I had to jerry-rig it.

I'm keeping the bags, because I do like the quick on-and-off feature. And they're good sized, and they look sharp. But with a few tweaks to the design they could've been perfect. They're not.
text_fidelity_b: Ibera Bicycle Bag PakRak Clip-On Quick-Release All Weather Bike Panniers (Pair), Includes Rain Cover , Black

TIMBUK2 Command Laptop Backpack, Black [[VIDEOID:mo363W3UY9IZ8Y3]]Let me start by saying that I've been using various Timbuk2's bags since the mid 1990s. While the prices may be a bit high, I've consistently found their bags to be well built, durable, with excellent water protection. In fact, I recently used one of their camera backpacks on a three week trip across Japan where the bag was subjected to a number of downpours; no water ever pierced the bag's envelope.

In terms of size, the volume of this bag is comparable to the laptop briefcases that came with laptops in the 1990s through the early aughts. As you'll see in my video, the laptop is housed in a compartment on the back of the bag in a heavily padded sleeve. In the video I have a 13" MacBook Pro in it.

There are two other compartments for storage and numerous small zipper pockets. On one side there is a water bottle holder, and on one of the shoulder straps a bottle opener (a standard feature of all Timbuk2 bags).

There's heavy padding on the back of the bag (where your back touches it) as well as on the shoulder straps.

As the the video shows, it's not a large bag, and that's the point. It's meant to hold your laptop and several documents -- whatever you may need to bring home from work for the night or the weekend. It's also small enough that if you're going out after work and you have it with you, it will easily fit under a table. And, it will fit under any airplane seat.

Finally, I also like that there's no indication that it's a laptop bag. In fact, if someone were going through it, they probably wouldn't even notice the laptop compartment in the back.
text_fidelity_b: TIMBUK2 Command Laptop Backpack, Black

Dynaplug Racer Pro Bicycle Tire Repair Tool 100% USA Made (Orange) I did the Unbound Gravel 200 and, like many others during the race, got a flat tire. The sharp Flint Hills rock sliced about a 3/8 in cut in my sidewall around 45 miles in. I run inserts in my tubeless tire setup, so I really didn’t want to have to put a tube in because (1) it is really hard to get the tire off and (2) I didn’t want to have to carry the sealant covered insert 30 miles until the next checkpoint.

I wasn’t sure if the Dynaplug would get the tire to seal or how long it would hold due to the size of the cut. I’ve had smaller sidewall cuts that regular bacon strips couldn’t fix. After using 2 plugs and spinning the wheel on its side a few times, I was very pleased to see the tire held air - and it held for the next 155 miles to the finish.

I highly recommend Dynaplug and especially the Racer Pro model that holds 4 plugs. I wouldn’t want to go on any epic rides with any lesser tool. It is on the expensive side, but it is worth the peace of mind and ease of use.
text_fidelity_b: Dynaplug Racer Pro Bicycle Tire Repair Tool 100% USA Made (Orange)

text_fidelity_a: Stanley Adventure Stainless Fry Pan Camp Cook Set, 9 Piece Camping Cookware Mess Kit with Stainless Pan, Cooking Utensils, and Dishes So many ways to consider camp cook gear. When I was young and fit and backpacked most weekends in the summer and autumn, the difference between stainless steel and titanium was that one metal warped more than the other and one weighed a bit less...but not enough to matter.  Both metals were uneven in the transfer of heat; foods stuck.  We 'loved' our stainless Sierrra Cups...but they were too hot on the lips...and cooled the contents too fast.  This Stanley product with its expanded poly cups provides extended warmth to beverages, soups or stews.  The metal pot has clearly visible volumetric markings.  The cup sits very well on folding alchohol or small wood burning stoves like the Firebox.  'Bug Out Kits' benefit from this setup:  we cannot rely on available wood but we need a pot to boil water and something to eat a small meal in...for two.

Old Timer Generational USA Series Traditional Fixed and Folding Knives with 1095 HC Stainless Steel Blades, Sawcut Bone Handles, and Made in USA for Hunting, Skinning, EDC, Field Dressing, and Outdoor I have not previously worked with Old Timer knives, though I have had my share of pocket knives that have served me well. So, this is my first experience with this brand and so far I am very pleased. This is a quality pocket knife, without a lot of frills and fancy features but very well made and attractive.

Most cheap pocket knives have a plastic handle, spring-assisted fly-out blade, and a locking mechanism. Beyond that the features become quite varied and bring different features to the table. That's all good, but anything beyond the basics - a blade in a case - adds weight and size. This knife is different. It keeps everything very simple - a single pull-out blade that locks. That's it.

The blade is solid and sharp right out of the package and is well suited for most tasks. There is no wobble in the blade and it remains stiff and tight, which is a good thing. The blade is free of pits and dings (at least initially) and is sharp enough to cut without pain (so be careful).

The handle is bone, not cheap plastic or resin. It has a nice, solid feel to it and it will last for decades with proper care. It also has eye appeal and is reminiscent of old-fashioned knives.

I am very pleased with this knife and will carry it instead of a larger cheap knife when I want a small, lightweight but well-made knife with me. I expect to get years of service from this knife.
text_fidelity_b: Old Timer Generational USA Series Traditional Fixed and Folding Knives with 1095 HC Stainless Steel Blades, Sawcut Bone Handles, and Made in USA for Hunting, Skinning, EDC, Field Dressing, and Outdoor

text_fidelity_a:
MSR SweetWater Microfilter While gravity filters have become the most popular backpacking water filters because no pumping is required, pump filters are still essential in situations where you only have access to shallow water sources. And that's why I went with the MSR SweetWater for a 5 night backpacking trip in the Grand Canyon backcountry — all of the water sources were shallow streams.

Pump filters aren't fast, but only having to filter 3 to 4 liters a day for myself really wasn't much of a chore. If this was the only filter for a group of people, then I'd say figure out a way to use a gravity filter.

I never got sick, so I suppose that's some kind of sign that the filter worked. It didn't, though, fully remove odors from the water. The water at one of the places I filled up had a slight swampy smell to it that was still there after I filtered.

The Nalgene attachment that it comes with is quite useful. The overall weight and size are also good for backpacking.

Note: You absolutely have to always use the prefilter. If you don't, tiny pebbles will get sucked in and obstruct the plunger. I don't get why MSR makes the prefilter an attachment rather than permanently part of the inhouse. Well, actually I guess they do that so you can replace the hose without also replacing the prefilter, but they're just inviting people to use the filter without the prefilter. Speaking from experience, if a pebble does get stuck in there it's not to hard to get it out. But always bring a backup filter.
text_fidelity_b: MSR SweetWater Microfilter

text_fidelity_a:
Sven-Saw 60th Anniversary Engraved 21" Folding Saw I bought this to replace a Corona folding saw in my off-road SUV. I use this saw primarily to clear branches that block the trail or to cut up trees or limbs that have fallen across the trail and are too big to pull clear. Even if I use the winch, some things need to but cut up so they will fit into where I want to pull them. I don't have room to always carry a gas-powered chainsaw, but a fast hand saw works great for wet wood up to 6 inches and dry (dead) wood possibly 8 to 10 inches thick. Bigger than that, I probably don't need to bother it.

My biggest reason for replacing the folding saw was that the particular one I had didn't sheild all the teeth of the curved blade within the wood handle. I didn't like the sharp saw teeth in my tool bag. A straight saw (with the handle in a straight line from the blade) doesn't give the best power, but this triangular design is the best of both worlds (folds straight, and opens to a large angle between the blade and handle).

The disadvantage of a frame saw like this is that you can run into the limit of the frame cutting through a thick piece. A panel saw (whether fixed or folding handle) can keep going indefinitely. Still, there are some practical limits imposed by how hard I want to work and how thick a piece is going to be while still being narrow enough that my saw length will span it. I feel confident the 21" frame saw will meet my needs. While a considerably smaller panel saw with no frame in the way would also do very well, the folding design of the Sven's frame is such that it has the advantage in compactness. The length won't fit in a tool bag, but the very thin design fits neatly under the rear bench seat in my SUV along with my other long tools (a 48" Hi-Lift bar and handle, an 18" socket handle, and spare 5/8 wave VHF antenna).

I added a washer between the wing-nut and saw handle. This provides a bearing surface for the wing nut which does not turn against the Aluminum handle.
text_fidelity_b: Sven-Saw 60th Anniversary Engraved 21" Folding Saw

text_fidelity_a:
Gym Timer with Remote, Alrigon LED Interval Timer Clock 1.5" Digits Down/Up Clock Stopwatch for Crossfit, Tabata, EMOM, MMA I got this timer for not only workouts, but also for using in organizing my time. I have to balance art work with home office work so I need to have a timer to help me not go over schedule for these different things. Let's take a look at this timer.

MANUAL
The manual that comes with this is very well laid out. I am extremely impressed with it. There are many photos which are helpful in the remote and wall installation as well as excellent information on how to run this timer in various modes.

LEARNING CURVE- GIVE YOURSELF TIME TO LEARN
I highly suggest that you take some time to learn this timer before you try to use it. I know that sounds silly, but there is a learning curve to this. I found it much nicer when I took the time to learn each function, play with it and then make notes in the manual. If you are already familiar with this type of timer, of course, then you probably won't need that.

CORDS
This came with TWO cords. One of them is a USB cord which is 3 ft long. That will plug into any USB port. The 2nd is a plug that has a transformer on the end. It is a sideways plug so it should fit on most power strips. That cord is only 68 inches long.

REMOTE
You will need two AAA batteries. This did not come with any. The manual has extensive instructions on how to set up and use the remote. They are very visual so visual learners will love this. It is IR and will work from across an average room, not sure about a large gym, however.

CLOCK
You can set this up as a real time clock and then use it as a timer so you don't have to unplug it when you are done. The timers all set up individually outside of the clock which keeps running in the background.

TIMER
The timer is easy to see from anywhere around my basement room or upstairs if I am using it in a room for other purposes. It does have a loud alarm on it too. I use the timer, Count Up and Count Down settings the most. I use interval timing when I want to follow a tight schedule during the day.

DOES IT PERFORM WELL?
I am very happy with this timer. I love that it has TWO cords so that I can put it on the table top when I am doing artwork. I can plug it into my USB outlet which is very close and then have the timer nearby. When I want to use this in the workout setting, I move it to my basement and either attach it to an outlet, or if I don't have one near where I want to use it, I use a power bank.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This timer is easy to see, great to operate, and extremely helpful in daily workouts or schedules. I am glad to have it and appreciate the work that went into the manual too. There is some learning to this timer, however. If you have never had one before, plan on taking some time to learn the set up.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great set up. I use this a lot.
text_fidelity_b: Gym Timer with Remote, Alrigon LED Interval Timer Clock 1.5" Digits Down/Up Clock Stopwatch for Crossfit, Tabata, EMOM, MMA

Hewolf Camping Sleeping Bag Waterproof - Compact Indoor Outdoor Sleeping Bags 4 Season Great for Adults Kids Youth Teen can be Zipped Together (Blue, Single 32-50F/0-10℃(1.8kg)-Right Zip) This bag arrives snugly packed in a compression bag that is small enough to easily pack into or strapped onto a backpack, either internal or external frame. Unpacking the bag from this sack was a bit of a challenge as the compression straps are sewn onto the sack and move just enough to get the bag out.

I was pleased with the way the bag looked, the outer shell is a slick navy and medium blue poly that does seem to be at least water resistant because when I poured a glass of water on it the water did bead up and did not soak into the bag. The interior is a grey, lighter weight and slightly brushed poly that feels much more pleasant than some sleeping bag interiors that i have used - not as slick. The zippers, and there are two, are a heavy nylon and have a grosgrain draft barrier on the inside. The long zipper on the side has metal tabs on both the inside and outside. There is an addition slide at the lower end of this zipper for further adjustments. A separate, similar zipper is across the bottom. The way the bottom is configured it appears as though the bag cannot be fully opened. Additionally there is a quarter inch or so gap between the two zippers at the corner so a very small amount of cold air might infiltrate.

There is a permanently attached hood on this bag. If not needed for warmth it can be quite wide and used as just a place to rest a pillow. In cold weather the hood can be drawn in quite snuggly by use of a drawstring. On the inside of the bag there is a soft sewn in tube to keep drafts from entering around the neck. There is also a clever little pocket on the inside near the neck just perfect for tucking a phone.

As for size - I am a woman, 5'6" and average weight and found the bag quite comfortable. It is tapered but roomier than a true mummy. I don't think this would be a good choice for anyone 6 feet tall or over, or for anyone more than a few pounds overweight.

I had no problem operating the drawstring, zippers, etc. Putting the bag back into the stuff sack was an average amount of trouble for returning a bag into a sack.

There is information printed on the stuff sack but it is in Chinese so I can only guess about what it says. The bit that I take to be a temperature comfort range indicates this as a warm weather bag 40 to 60 degrees Fahrenheit, although 0 Celsius is mentioned (32 Fahrenheit). If sleeping without a shelter and with minimal ground cover the 50 to 60 would be correct, with appropriate ground cover (pad, ground sheet etc) it could go lower, and with a tent down to just above freezing should be fine.

This is an inexpensive bag but surprisingly well made considering the modest price and filled with some features usually reserved for more expensive bags. Besides the ones mentioned there are tabs on the bottom so the bag can easily be hung up to dry or air out. Also this bag comes in right or left zips, and two bags, (one of each configuration) can be zipped together - making this an excellent choice for couples. Even though the bag is not particularly generously cut but it would be an excellent choice for a child/young teen to take to camp, particularly if sleeping in a tent.
text_fidelity_b: Hewolf Camping Sleeping Bag Waterproof - Compact Indoor Outdoor Sleeping Bags 4 Season Great for Adults Kids Youth Teen can be Zipped Together (Blue, Single 32-50F/0-10℃(1.8kg)-Right Zip)
